Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.
n7addc66065b1: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is a key antiviral target that equilibrates between an active dimer and inactive monomer, making the dimerization interface a promising therapeutic vulnerability. This study investigates Mpro monomer-dimer equilibrium and conformational changes induced by inhibitor binding using 13C labeling with native mass spectrometry and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). We evaluated how peptidomimetic inhibitors (PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, boceprevir) and non-peptidomimetic inhibitors (carmofur, ebselen, MR6-31-2, AT7519, pelitinib) influence Mpro dimerization and subunit exchange. Key findings revealed divergent mechanisms: peptidomimetic inhibitors significantly shifted the equilibrium towards the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange dynamics and rigidifying the dimer interface; in contrast, ebselen impaired dimer formation and increased interface flexibility. Notably, tandem mass spectrometry identified a novel covalent binding site for ebselen at C300. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses demonstrated that this C300 modification allosterically alters the hydrogen bond network of the dimer interface, directly contributing to ebselen-mediated dimer disruption and enzymatic inhibition. Overall, this study clarifies distinct inhibitory modes between peptidomimetics and ebselen, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting allosteric sites at the dimer interface for designing next-generation Mpro inhibitors.
n6c8eb0508434: The evolutionary arms race between plants and insects involves not only direct defense and counter-defense but also sophisticated resource manipulation. However, how herbivorous insects respond to host nutritional signals to modulate their fitness traits remains unclear. This study investigates how the small brown planthopper (SBPH, Laodelphax striatellus) manipulates host plant carbohydrate allocation, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the acquired glucose enhances SBPH fecundity and insecticide tolerance. Using molecular, pharmacological, and biochemical approaches, we found that SBPH infestation induced systemic carbohydrate reallocation in rice, elevating whole-plant glucose levels by promoting aerial accumulation while depleting root reserves. Host-derived glucose enhanced SBPH fecundity by activating the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, upregulating juvenile hormone (JH) signaling, and increasing vitellogenin production. For imidacloprid tolerance, glucose boosted glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity via two synergistic mechanisms: by upregulating glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to increase glutathione synthesis, and transcriptionally via the glucose-TOR-JH axis to induce LsGSTe1 (SBPH epsilon class GST) and LsGSTo1 (SBPH omega class GST) expression. Our findings establish host-derived glucose as a central signaling molecule that SBPH utilizes to modulate conserved pathways for simultaneous optimization of reproduction and insecticide resistance. This reveals a multifaceted nutrient-responsive mechanism in insect pests and identifies the glucose-TOR-JH axis as critical molecular targets for developing nutrient-based pest control strategies, such as disrupting insect nutrient-sensing pathways or modulating host carbohydrate metabolism.
n2d3bfbd3d4b4: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH (https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/, https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.
n88df928e4c65: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.
n9a95df70102a: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.
n655877e57217: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.
nfd78a74cc8d9: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.
n789e4ad2e301: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.
nbe59f49b00ea: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.
n0147da51a5b2: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.
n01db1bbde499: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.
n0c668217e858: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.
n6bce9b30997a: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.
n1244691a4e1e: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21REINS) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21REINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.
nd029882b919f: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.
nf4f0b11fa06c: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral–caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.
na3412ebfff91: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.
nae30eedf1261: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.
n0ab99943e7ed: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. Here, we identify factors suppressing Th17 responses during primary infection. We demonstrate that the lack of Th17 induction is independent of route and duration. Next, using Tbx21-deficient mice, we show that Mtb drives a Th1 response that is only partially protective and limits Th17 cell production in an IFN-γ-independent manner. We further reveal that the ESX-1 type VII secretion system and lipid phthiocerol dimycocerosate (PDIM) suppress Th17 responses. Infection with ESX-1 or PDIM mutants results in significantly increased Th17 T cells and IL-17A cytokine in the lungs, and infection of IL-17A-deficient animals partially restores virulence of ESX-1 and PDIM mutants. Although the ESX-1 secretion system and lipid PDIM elicit type I IFN, which can suppress Th17 differentiation, we find that suppression of Th17 is independent of type I IFN. Instead, ESX-1 and PDIM suppress production of IL-23, a cytokine that promotes Th17 differentiation, in dendritic cells found in mediastinal lymph nodes during Mtb infection. These findings define a new function of the ESX-1 secretion system and PDIM in Mtb virulence, a long-standing question in tuberculosis research.
n089630dc6e4b: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women’s health.
n982e6e4d7d55: In this autobiography, I describe my childhood and early education and summarize structural biology research in nucleic acids and proteins and my work with the Protein Data Bank.
ncea4acd33b2d: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.
n7f3c4ea9b936: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 (“Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals”). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.
n17874f8e9c9d: The steroid hormone dafachronic acid may carry the effects of reduced mTOR activity between tissues to coordinate metabolism and longevity across the body.
n601bcd0527b0: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. Motor units, each of which consists of a single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates, contribute to the total activation of each muscle through their recruitment and firing rate when active. However, it remains unknown how the nervous system controls locomotor speed by changing the firing of individual motor units. To address this, we combined quantitative behavioral analysis of mouse locomotion with single motor unit recordings from the lateral and long heads of the triceps brachii, which drive monoarticular extension of the elbow and biarticular movements of the elbow and shoulder, respectively. In contrast to prior studies employing bulk electromyography (EMG) to examine muscle activity, our recordings revealed the diversity of spike patterning across motor units, as well as systematic differences in motor unit activity across muscles and locomotor speeds. First, motor unit activity differed significantly across the lateral and long heads, suggesting differential control of these two closely apposed elbow extensor muscles. Second, we found that individual units were recruited probabilistically (during only a subset of strides), showing that the highly repeatable bulk EMG signals observed across strides, in fact, reflect varying subsets of individual motor units. Finally, although recruitment probability and firing rate both increased at faster walking speeds, increases in recruitment were proportionally larger than rate changes, and recruitment of individual units accompanied changes in limb kinematics. Together, these results reveal how the firing of individual motor units varies systematically across muscles and walking speeds to produce flexible locomotor behavior.
n52da83b80ad0: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. We have used whole-network Ca2+ imaging to study olfactory coding in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that the odorant 1-octanol is encoded combinatorially in the periphery as both an attractant and a repellent. These inputs are integrated centrally, and their relative strengths determine the sensitivity and valence of the behavioral response through modulation of locomotory reversals and speed. The balance of these pathways also dictates the activity of the locomotory command interneurons, which control locomotory reversals. This balance serves as a regulatory node for response modulation, allowing C. elegans to weigh opportunities and hazards in its environment when formulating behavioral responses. Thus, an odorant can be encoded simultaneously as inputs of opposite valence, focusing attention on the integration of these inputs in determining perception, response, and plasticity.
n6808a24d9bca: As elsewhere in the world, archaeological records in eastern Africa show that long environmental variabilities shaped the emergence and development of farming economies. Marine sediments and isotopic data indicate alternating humid and arid phases that coincide with the reorganization of settlements, establishment of agricultural landscapes, and the generation of new subsistence practices during the later Holocene. Strengthened monsoons during the African Humid Period (13,050–3050 BCE) produced environments that enabled human mobility, likely experimentation with plants, and the dispersal of early herders through the Rift Valley and the Horn of Africa. Archaeological, archaeobotanical, isotopic, and other data from sites in the Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, and elsewhere indicate varied and gradual transitions from foraging to mixed farming, shaped by microenvironments, altitude, and intercommunity exchanges. Case studies of farming systems developed over the last 2,000 years demonstrate innovative forms of resilient landscape engineering and complex social management. We suggest that the equity and collective stewardship attested by this record offer valuable analogues for contemporary climate adaptation in the Anthropocene.
n1ac9129e894b: This reflection on my years in linguistic anthropology also includes the broader sociohistorical transformations of which I have been a part. The Cold War and its aftermath were the backdrop against which we learned and taught. As a child migrant to the United States from the Soviet region, I became fascinated by the intersection of political relationships and linguistic practices. At the same time, linguistic anthropology was starting to navigate between theories of political economy and the analysis of speaking as action-in-events. Within that endeavor, I have studied conceptual questions about multilingualism and the workings of language ideology as well as questions about sign phenomena in constructing gender, sociocultural differentiation, scaling, and translation. My scholarly path has depended on the generous, inspiring influence of mentors, colleagues, and students, individually and in the many seminars and study groups we have formed together. Working now on analyzing authoritarian regimes, I see with alarm their effects on public expression, safety, and protest, echoing my earliest memories of repression.
nc37ea52f64d4: How anthropologists have invoked and conceptualized anxiety reflects the development of new ways of relating selfhood, subjectivity, and the sociopolitical to each other. This article examines the recent development of anthropological frameworks of anxiety in the context of the rising prevalence of and interest in anxiety. Since its inception in modern social theory, anxiety has functioned as a commentary on people's relation to risk, precarity, and emerging forms of capitalism. Early anthropological approaches to anxiety relied extensively on psychological theories that focused on the emotions at an individual level. Although they framed anxiety as a social condition in addition to an inner one, they were still beholden to the politics and ethics of the sovereign subject and dichotomies between self and society, individual and collective, and citizen and state. By framing anxiety as a social practice and relation, contemporary anthropologists are now redefining anxiety's role in political-economic transformations from a passive reflection of widespread uncertainty and insecurity to an agentive constituent of politics itself.
nb7d681096d2b: A review of the anthropological literature motivates an expansive definition of the therapeutic as practices that have or are purported to have salubrious effects on at least one of the parties involved. Those effects could be on the psychic or spiritual state of participants (i.e., what one is or has), on how they make sense of their state or circumstances (i.e., how one sees, feels, understands, or knows), and/or on their behavior (i.e., what one does and says, how, and to what effect). The idea that the therapeutic is invariably a matter of communicative practice is a premise of this review, which addresses ( a ) the diversity and distinctiveness of therapies as multimodal genres; ( b ) the therapeutic distillation of cultural values, projects, and ideals; ( c ) the epistemic and interpretive challenges of therapeutic communication, particularly relative to politically loaded questions of mediation; and ( d ) the scaling of the therapeutic as a kind of communication by way of communication.
n86ff13de8d4a: This article provides an overview of experimental anthropology, arguing that, from its inception, anthropology has operated as a form of experimental inquiry aimed at producing a surplus of data, relations, and sensations. We explore this notion through a tripartite heuristic for understanding how anthropological creativity draws on methods from the natural sciences as well as from art and design: ( a ) experience-based experimentation, ( b ) the adoption of scientific protocols and instruments, and ( c ) experimentation with and through models. Despite the apparent diversity of contemporary approaches, efforts to reimagine experimentalism in anthropology can still be understood through this heuristic. We revisit it in reverse order, arguing, first, that modeling now takes place through prototypes, games, devices, and other relational infrastructures; second, that apparatus-based experimentation has opened new possibilities for sensory enrichment; and finally, that anthropological practice itself emerges as a radical venture that expands conceptual, physical, and existential boundaries, with ethnographic inquiry relentlessly generating excess data.
n727fc55c624a: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.
ncfa127a7cc72: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.
n4e9b434f9b80: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. As part of a broader Registered Report series, this study examined whether a longitudinal intervention designed to strengthen psychological correlates of pro-environmental behaviour could motivate n = 31 university students in The Netherlands to take climate action. The intervention was delivered over six weeks through interactive lessons and activities informed by psychological theories and interventions. The goal was to increase pro-climate behaviours by targeting 12 psychological factors. Participants completed surveys assessing these correlates, as well as ecological momentary assessments of individual and collective pro-climate behaviours before and after the intervention, and after three months (14 days each). A control group was included (n = 27). Results showed that 4 of the 12 psychological correlates increased significantly: emotional engagement, collective efficacy, the bottom-up theory of change (the belief that change can start from grassroots action and spread systemically) and climate appraisal. Three (except appraisal) remained elevated at the three-month follow-up. Civic engagement, advocacy and activism increased after the intervention in the experimental group relative to control group. The increase in activist behaviour was predicted by the development of a bottom-up theory of change.
n4993b2be88a7: Understanding the taxonomic affinity of putative avialan teeth is essential to assessing the geographic range and richness of Late Cretaceous toothed birds. Isolated teeth attributed to Avialae are known from numerous North American Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages. However, because only a select few of these tooth types are known from teeth preserved in jaws, their taxonomic affinities remain uncertain. Several key morphologies used to diagnose avialan teeth are also present in non-avialan theropods and crocodyliforms, leading some to question whether many such isolated teeth belong to birds. Here, we provide detailed descriptions and high-resolution images of avialan teeth from the Late Cretaceous Prince Creek Formation (PCF) of northern Alaska. A total of 105 isolated teeth were identified as avialan and can be divided into seven distinct morphotypes. Crucially, decades of extensive microfossil sampling have failed to produce any evidence of crocodyliforms in the PCF, allowing us to rule out this possible identity. Further, the teeth described here can be distinguished from those of all non-avialan theropods known in the PCF. Our morphotypes thus provide an important framework for identifying bird teeth in other Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages as well as understanding avialan diversity before the K–Pg extinction.
n760d688f9262: Hybrid quantum–classical machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices suffers from three coupled overheads: hardware miscalibration, classical syndrome-decoding latency and shot noise on gradient estimators. We present quantum calibration and observable processing (QCOP), a unified closed-loop control layer integrating a spectral calibration engine (SCE), a hierarchical syndrome decoder (HSD) and an observable compression layer (OCL) within a single GPU-accelerated pipeline. Three theoretical bounds characterize the joint effect on logical error rate (LER), convergence rate and observable variance. On device-calibrated noise-model simulators (n=20 seeds), QCOP achieves up to 2× wall-clock training speed-up and approximately 40% variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) energy error reduction relative to the unaugmented baseline. A hardware pilot on ibm_nairobi at surface-code distance d=5 (2000 syndrome volumes, 8192 shots each, single calibration window) yields a 1.6× latency reduction and 1.9× LER reduction for the HSD over minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM)—directionally consistent with simulation but quantitatively smaller, indicating noise sources beyond the model. This pilot exercises the HSD alone: the SCE and the OCL have not been run on physical hardware, and the three modules have never been executed jointly on a device. The end-to-end QCOP benefits—speed-up, energy error reduction and variance reduction—are therefore not hardware-validated, and end-to-end hardware validation of all three modules remains future work. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/hekimoghlu/QCOP.
nf33364b8015d: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.
na1ff310586e8: Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.
neb1570ec24da: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children’s, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.
n05c6c4984c30: In human language, word order impacts how words are categorized and understood (as nouns, verbs etc.). We have demonstrated that this effect extends to non-linguistic stimuli, suggesting that the impact of sequence order on stimulus categorization is a domain-general, rather than language-specific cognitive process. Here, we ask if this process is evolutionarily conserved in other non-human primates. We developed a non-linguistic experiment and tested rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and bonobos (Pan paniscus). Participants first learned to categorize shapes (as rounded, squared or pointed). We next assessed how they categorized ambiguous morph shapes by combining exemplars from each category. We provided sequential information by training the animals to select shapes in a specified order: rounded, then squared and then pointed. Finally, we assessed whether presentation in specific positions in this learned sequence would impact subsequent categorization of ambiguous morph shapes. In humans, an ambiguous morph was more likely to be categorized as the shape it replaced in a sequence. Non-human primates, however, showed no such effect, categorizing stimuli independent of their position in a sequence. This suggests that the tendency to infer category membership from sequence order is not shared across primates, and may have evolved more recently in the human lineage.
nbd05594d8f94: Mirror life presents a low-likelihood but high-severity global biosecurity threat that has attracted the attention of bioscientists, governments and international security organizations. However, current analytical techniques are not fit to identify mirror life biohazards. Herein, we propose the first assay method for screening against mirror life. This approach is based upon optical circularly polarized luminesce (CPL) signatures generated by fluorescent probes, which bind to subcellular targets (e.g. membranes, organelles, nucleic acids, etc.). Probes can either be achiral or be intrinsically chiral. We set out why a multi-probe reporter panel approach incorporating many CPL-generating probes is necessary to identify mirror life with a high degree of confidence (i.e. avoiding false positives). The distinct CPL signatures can be analysed via recent innovations in CPL detection, i.e. rapid CPL spectroscopy, CPL microscopy (enantioselective differential chiral contrast, EDCC, imaging) and CPL EDCC cameras. While these are advanced technologies, they share the same fundamental optical principles as three-dimensional cinema glasses and so are amenable to scaling and portable applications. The CPL assay approach to mirror life screening could be a useful tool for screening against mirror life biohazards and ensuring compliance with any potential future international legislation against mirror-life research.
ne6f5460adcac: We propose an iterative programmatic planning (IPP) framework that solves grid-based tasks by using large language models (LLMs) to synthesize interpretable, executable programs that act as agent policies mapping environment states to action sequences, rather than relying on traditional search or reinforcement learning. Alongside prompting strategies such as direct code generation, pseudocode conditioned refinement and curriculum-based prompting, IPP centres on an iterative refinement mechanism that updates code from coarse, task-level feedback. We evaluate our approach using six leading LLMs and two challenging grid-based benchmarks (grid-based reasoning for assessing spatial planning (GRASP) and MiniGrid). Our IPP framework demonstrates improvements over direct code generation for five of the six models, with net energy gains ranging from a few per cent to roughly threefold and, for Gemini-2.5-Pro, a sign flip from a negative baseline to a strongly positive score, establishes a new state-of-the-art result for GRASP and significantly outperforms direct elicitation from GPT-o3-mini (by 43% on the hardest MiniGrid task to 116% on GRASP). While code generation has a higher initial prompting cost compared to direct solution elicitation ($0.08 per task versus $0.002 per instance for GPT-o3-mini), the code can be reused for any number of instances, making the amortized cost significantly lower (by 400 times on GPT-o3-mini across the complete GRASP benchmark). Beyond performance gains, IPP produces reusable, human-readable policies that support transparent inspection and modification, underscoring the advantages of planning as program synthesis over per-instance inference. The code and results can be found at http://github.com/Mystic-Slice/LLM-Planning-CodeGen.
n3476bd0108c4: The Neogene fossil record of Patagonia provides important insights into the evolution and ecological diversification of marine predators in the Southern Hemisphere. Among these, Kawas benegasorum, an extinct seal from the Late Miocene Puerto Madryn Formation, represents the only record of a putative phocine (northern seals) in the Southern Hemisphere and preserves rare evidence of stomach contents. However, its original description was concise, and lacked detailed information on its dentition and stomach contents, leaving aspects of its morphology, phylogeny and paleoecology unresolved. We re-describe the holotype and only known specimen of K. benegasorum, providing the first comprehensive study of its postcranial morphology, new information on its dentition and a detailed examination of its stomach contents. We show that Kawas has both monachine- and phocine-like traits, with an overall morphology suggesting affinities with Monachinae. However, phylogenetic analyses yielded conflicting results, recovering Kawas either within Phocinae or in an unresolved position within Phocidae. The stomach contents indicate a piscivorous diet with coastal, benthic and demersal prey, broadly comparable to that of extant South American sea lions inhabiting the region. These results document early benthic nearshore foraging in pinnipeds and suggest dietary convergence across geological time in the western South Atlantic by the Late Miocene.
n3489e2461cca: Several species rely on mechanisms to resolve conflicts and reduce their negative consequences, including reconciliation and third-party affiliation (i.e. post-conflict affiliative interactions between victims and aggressors, and between victims and third parties, respectively). Here, we studied reconciliation and third-party affiliation in two groups of wolves (n = 20) and three groups of wolves introgressed with dogs (i.e. second- or later-generation backcrosses of wolf-dog hybrids to wolves; n = 13), in captivity. We conducted behavioural observations of post-conflict affiliative interactions using continuous focal sampling for 2 minutes following an aggression, and during matched-control periods. Our results showed that both admixed and non-admixed wolves engaged in post-conflict affiliation consistent with reconciliation and third-party affiliation. Although we found no evidence that admixed wolves showed lower reconciliation or third-party affiliation than non-admixed wolves, social factors had different modulatory effects in admixed and non-admixed wolves. In particular, stronger social bonds promoted post-conflict affiliation in non-admixed wolves, whereas greater rank distance was associated with higher post-conflict affiliation in admixed wolves. Moreover, post-conflict affiliation was more likely following high-intensity aggression in both admixed and non-admixed wolves, and after unidirectional conflicts in the latter. These findings indicate that dog introgression may influence post-conflict behaviour in wolves and suggest that, while both admixed and non-admixed wolves engage in post-conflict affiliation, the mechanisms underlying them may partially differ.
n278be3486cb3: Pathogens exert strong selective pressure on group-living primates. In humans, disease defence includes both a biological and behavioural immune system, which includes the emotion of disgust and avoidance behaviours shaped by genetics, learning and culture. While pathogen avoidance is documented in nonhuman primates, little is known about how ecological and developmental factors influence pathogen sensitivity, that is, individual variation in pathogen avoidance. We conducted two studies to examine this in macaques. Our first study tested macaques (n = 54) from seven different species and four different rearing backgrounds in a visual food-choice task where food was either placed on a substrate with or without pathogenic cues. Macaques preferred feeding on non-contaminated substrates, with sanctuary-born individuals showing greater avoidance than former pets. Our second study tested sanctuary-born Japanese macaques (n = 55) from four groups; three groups had recently experienced an infectious disease outbreak. Macaques from exposed groups showed significantly higher avoidance of contaminated substrates. Together, our findings suggest that early life rearing experience and recent disease exposure shape pathogen sensitivity in macaques, demonstrating a flexible behavioural immune system in Old World monkeys. These findings suggest that flexible, context-sensitive pathogen avoidance is present in Old World monkeys, providing the behavioural foundations from which human disgust may have evolved.
n5cc5b50de041: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems, including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on the prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.
n92841ace8bd1: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.
